title: RNA Extraction with Trizol for Tissues
author: Maysa Silva
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.stmeek6

steps.title: Homogenize Tissue
steps.instruction: Homogenize 50 to 100 mg of tissue with 1 mL of Trizol using a homogenizer and transfer to a tube.

substeps.instruction: Optionally, freeze the sample at -80°C for up to 6 months.

steps.title: Dissociate Nucleoprotein Complex
steps.instruction: Incubate the sample for 5 minutes to allow complete dissociation of the nucleoproteins complex.

steps.title: Phase Separation
steps.instruction: Add 200 μL of chloroform per 1 mL of TRIzol and incubate for 2 to 3 minutes.

steps.title: Centrifuge for Phase Partitioning
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the sample for 15 minutes at 12,000 × g at 4°C.

steps.title: Recover Aqueous Phase
steps.instruction: Transfer the colorless upper aqueous phase containing the RNA to a new tube by angling the tube at 45° and pipetting the solution out.

steps.title: Precipitate RNA
steps.instruction: Add 500 μL of isopropanol per 1 mL of TRIzol and incubate for 10 minutes.

steps.title: Pellet RNA
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the sample for 10 minutes at 12,000 × g at 4°C.

steps.title: Wash RNA Pellet
steps.instruction: Discard the supernatant with a micropipette and resuspend the pellet in 1 mL of 75% ethanol per 1 mL of TRIzol.

steps.title: Centrifuge and Dry Pellet
steps.instruction: Vortex the sample briefly and centrifuge for 5 minutes at 7,500 × g at 4°C.

substeps.instruction: Discard the supernatant with a micropipettor.
Vacuum or air dry the RNA pellet for 5–10 minutes.

steps.title: Resuspend RNA
steps.instruction: Resuspend the pellet by pipetting up and down in 20–50 µL of RNase-free water, 0.1 mM EDTA, or 0.5% SDS solution.

substeps.instruction: Note: Do not use 0.5% SDS if the RNA is intended for subsequent enzymatic reactions.

steps.title: Final Incubation and Storage
steps.instruction: Incubate the sample in a water bath or heat block set at 55–60°C for 10–15 minutes, then store in a -80°C freezer.
